```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

# Set global options
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE
)

# Load required libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(robotoolbox)
library(readxl)
library(labelled)

# Define OWD color palette
owd_palette <- c("#5b195b", "#9b2c60", "#ce525b",
                 "#f08453", "#ffbd54", "#f9f871")

background_color <- "#f5f5f2"
```

```{r}
#| label: load-data

form_id <- "ashaEDvw4ZLwGi9bqXGeqb"
form_file <- here::here("registration_form.xlsx")

# fetch data from Kobo with robotoolbox
raw_data <- kobo_data(x = form_id,
                      all_versions = TRUE)

# read in questionnaire and labels from XLS form
questionnaire <- read_xlsx(form_file,
                           sheet = "survey")

label_dict <- read_xlsx(form_file,
                        sheet = "choices")
```

```{r}
#| label: browser-usage
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-cap: "Browser usage among course participants"

# Process browser data
browser_data <- raw_data |>
  select(web_browser) |>
  filter(!is.na(web_browser))
```


```{r}
#| label: browser-plot
#| eval: false
# Create browser usage plot
browser_plot <- browser_data |>
  count(web_browser) |>
  mutate(percentage = n / sum(n) * 100,
         label = paste0(n, " (", round(percentage, 1), "%)")) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(web_browser, n), y = n, fill = web_browser)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_text(aes(label = label), hjust = -0.1, size = 3.5, fontface = "bold") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(x = "Browser",
       y = "Number of participants",
       title = "Web browser preferences in ds4owd-002") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none",
        plot.background = element_rect(fill = background_color, color = NA),
        panel.background = element_rect(fill = background_color, color = NA)) +
  #scale_fill_manual(values = owd_palette) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.25)))

print(browser_plot)
```


```{r}
# Get Chrome percentage for use in text
chrome_percentage <- browser_data |>
  count(web_browser) |>
  mutate(percentage = n / sum(n) * 100) |>
  filter(web_browser == "google_chrome") |>
  pull(percentage) |>
  round(0)
```


## Organize your digital workspace

Throughout this course, you'll be frequently accessing various websites and platforms. Setting up a well-organized bookmark system will save you time and help you stay focused on learning data science rather than searching for links.

::: {.callout-note}
## Chrome-focused instructions
Based on our course registration data, approximately `r chrome_percentage`% of participants use Google Chrome. These instructions are written specifically for Chrome users. If you're using a different browser, the general concepts still apply but menu locations and keyboard shortcuts may differ.
:::

## Step 1: Create a dedicated bookmarks folder in Chrome

1. Open Chrome.

![](images/bookmarks/screenshot-chrome-open.png){width=100%}

2. Click on the *three dots menu* in the top-right corner.

![](images/bookmarks/screenshot-three-dots-menu.png){width=100%}

3. Click on *Bookmarks and Lists*

![](images/bookmarks/screenshot-bookmarks-and-lists.png){width=100%}

4. Click on *Show Bookmarks Bar*. A bookmarks bar appears below the address bar in your browser. It might have already been there.

![](images/bookmarks/screenshot-show-bookmarks-bar.png){width=100%}

5. Right-click on the bookmarks bar and select *Add Folder...*.

![](images/bookmarks/screenshot-add-folder.png){width=100%}

6. Name the folder `ds4owd-002` in the Name files. Ensure that in the window below, *Bookmarks Bar* is selected as the location.

![](images/bookmarks/screenshot-name-folder.png){width=100%}

7. Click *Save*.

![](images/bookmarks/screenshot-save-folder.png){width=100%}

8. The folder `ds4owd-002` should now appear in your bookmarks bar.

![](images/bookmarks/screenshot-folder-created.png){width=100%}

## Step 2: Add course website to your folder

1. Navigate to the course website: [{{< var course.website >}}]({{< var course.website >}})

2. Click the *star icon* in the address bar. 

3. In the popup, add *course website* for the Name filed.

4. Click the *Folder* dropdown and select your `ds4owd-002` folder.

5. Click *Done*.

6. Click on your `ds4owd-002` folder in the bookmarks bar to verify the bookmark was added.

## Step 4: Create sub-folders for better organization in Chrome *(optional)*

As the course progresses, organize your Chrome bookmarks with sub-folders:

1. Right-click on your [ds4owd-002]{.highlight-yellow} folder
3. Select [Add new folder]{.highlight-yellow}
3. Create these sub-folders:
   - [Assignments]{.highlight-yellow} - for your personal assignment repositories
   - [Resources]{.highlight-yellow} - for R documentation, package sites
   - [Data]{.highlight-yellow} - for openwashdata and other data sources

### Recommended additional bookmarks

Add these to your [Resources]{.highlight-yellow} sub-folder:

- **R for Data Science book**: <https://r4ds.hadley.nz/>
- **ggplot2 documentation**: <https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/>
- **RStudio cheatsheets**: <https://posit.co/resources/cheatsheets/>
- **openwashdata**: <https://openwashdata.org/>

## Tipps

::: {.callout-tip}
## Sync Chrome bookmarks across devices
To sync your bookmarks across all your devices:
1. Click your [profile icon]{.highlight-yellow} in the top-right corner of Chrome
2. Click [Turn on sync]{.highlight-yellow}
3. Sign in with your Google account
4. Your ds4owd-002 bookmarks will now be available on all devices where you're signed into Chrome
:::
